target.title: feat(android): add safe cron job management
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw for Android could list cron jobs and show basic details, but it could not safely manage them. Operators had to switch to another client to inspect history, run a job, edit it, enable or disable it, or delete it.

This clean maintainer replacement supersedes #101882 after a protocol, concurrency, authorization, and accessibility rewrite. It preserves @snowzlmbot's contribution through commit co-authorship.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Add typed Android models for cron details, history, mutation patches, and the closed `cron.run` result variants.
- Send minimal `cron.update` patches so untouched gateway-owned fields remain intact; explicit model and thinking clears remain explicit nulls.
- Keep detail and history generations independent so stale responses cannot overwrite a newly selected job.
- Serialize mutations and retain the busy state through the awaited list refresh, preventing the UI from presenting a second action while the runtime mutex is still locked.
- Scope delete cleanup to the job actually deleted, so deleting one job cannot clear a newer selection or history request.
- Gate mutation controls on `operator.admin` while preserving read-only detail/history access, with truthful guidance for requesting and approving admin access.
- Add persistent visible labels, accessibility semantics, disabled styling, and admin/busy gating to every editor control.
- Validate command payload arguments as JSON strings and represent unsupported working-directory clearing explicitly instead of sending an invalid patch.
- Hoist editor drafts above transient detail loading, preserve unsaved values across reconnects, and compare editable configuration rather than runtime timestamps before declaring conflicts.
- Retain unbounded editor payloads only in the Activity-scoped ViewModel, never in Android saved-instance Binder state; rotation keeps the draft while process death and ordinary navigation clear it safely.
- Expose delete-after-run only for one-shot schedules and clear it when switching to a recurring schedule, matching the Gateway deletion contract.
- Block stale saves when the gateway changes the same job, require an explicit Revert, and keep retry available after transient detail-load failures.

## User Impact

Android Settings now supports cron job details, run history, run now, editing, enable/disable, and deletion. Read-scoped connections can inspect jobs and history; mutation controls become available only with admin scope. Run results distinguish completed, queued, skipped, and rejected outcomes instead of reporting every response as success.

## Evidence

Current reviewed head: `e124e836255`.

- Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kx3sp2wmc37meyk0ts6eeg52`: Play and third-party `CronJobDetailTest`, `CronJobManagementTest`, `CronRuntimeGuardTest`, `GatewayNodeApprovalStateTest`, `MainViewModelTest`, and `SettingsScreensTest` passed; Android ktlint and Play debug assembly passed.
- Native i18n inventory regenerated against current `main`; exact snapshot check reported 2,864 entries with no drift.
- Play debug APK SHA-256: `edc50861071478c4306af214352b81ac0208d27dd747e5b8a90100257e204064`; archive integrity clean.
- Fresh structured AutoReview: clean on the complete current-main branch after the saved-state and one-shot auto-delete fixes.
- Independent gateway/protocol review: clean after fixing selection-safe delete cleanup and admin recovery guidance.
- Independent Android UI review: clean after fixing mutation-state lifetime, same-millisecond conflict detection, disconnect/error recovery, all-control disablement, command argument validation, and field accessibility.
- API 36 behavior validation and exact-head hosted CI: in progress.

## Risk / Rollback

Risk is limited to Android cron Settings and its Gateway RPC projections. The Gateway remains the authorization authority. Rollback removes the Android management panel and typed mutation helpers without changing the Gateway protocol or stored cron jobs.
